title: Bug spec — ONE developer-facing spec, two renderers (board ticket + Sheet row)
description: The input of QA-Documentation/Bug-Reports/template/tools: redmine-bug.mjs renders it into the team's Textile board ticket, and bug-row.mjs renders THE SAME file into the v2 one-cell Sheet row (Bug Reports tab or, with --candidates, the Bug candidates funnel). One spec, both outputs — no second source of truth. This is deliberately NOT bug.schema.json: the QA RECORD carries the internal taxonomy (severity, P0–P3, invariants, tags); the spec carries only what a developer needs to reproduce, written in the language of their tool (REDMINE_WORKFLOW §Perspective by layer). Instances live at <Project>/QA-Documentation/bugs/BUG-NNN.redmine.json.

id.description: The QA record id. Optional for the board (the ticket gets a Redmine number), load-bearing for the Sheet: bug-row.mjs upserts by '<id> — <subject>' in column A, so a renamed id creates a duplicate row instead of updating one. A CANDIDATE (funnel draft, not yet a QA record) uses 'C-<n>' with an optional split letter ('C-7a'/'C-7b' — one row = one filing).

subject.description: WITHOUT any [BUG-…] prefix — the renderer derives the prefix from `layer`. Then '<what> <where>'; the build suffix comes from `build`, never typed here.

layer.description: Defect layer → subject prefix: App → [BUG-App], BE → [BUG-BE], FE → [BUG-FE]; absent → plain [BUG]. Also dictates the WORDING perspective (user journey vs exact API calls) — REDMINE_WORKFLOW §Perspective by layer.

build.description: Build number when the team's build numbering applies — renders as the subject suffix '(Directly on the <build> build)'.

priority.description: The REDMINE priority scale (default Normal), not the QA record's P0–P3 — the two scales answer different questions and are never mixed.

preconditions.description: USER perspective for App/FE (install build + log in), API perspective for BE (environment + auth + entity ids).

steps.description: Numbered by the renderers. UI journey for App/FE; the exact METHOD /endpoint calls for BE.

actual.description: SHORT and precise — one fact. What the user SEES (App/FE) or what the RESPONSE holds (BE).

screenshots.description: Evidence LINKS (file-host, e.g. Mega) — never local paths (those go in `attachments`). A bare string renders with the generic 'Screenshot:' label; a {label, url} pair renders the label as its own bold paragraph (board) / as the link text itself (Sheet). A placeholder url (`<Mega link …>`) renders as a bold label, never a broken link.

notes.description: Free facts for the assignee (debug ids, scope observations, dev suggestions). NO internal cross-references into the QA Sheet.

comments.description: Sheet-only (bug-row.mjs column C) — free info for the QA tab; never enters the board ticket.

attachments.description: LOCAL file paths uploaded INTO the Redmine issue (redmine-bug.mjs only). Links belong in `screenshots`.

assignee.description: Member name or numeric id — resolved against the board's membership; re-ask the responsibility roles per project.

sprint.description: "active" is the standard — the tool resolves the currently ACTIVE sprint LIVE at creation time; a name or id pins one explicitly. No active sprint on the board → the tool errors out, never guesses.

status.description: Omit = 'To do' in both renderers ('Backlog' only for very minor bugs, set explicitly). The first nine are the BOARD workflow (redmine-bug.mjs); 'QA in Progress'/'Reopen'/'Fixed' exist only in the Sheet tab's column-D lifecycle (bug-row.mjs) and the board tool refuses them.

verdict.description: Candidates funnel only (bug-row.mjs --candidates, column D; default Proposed). Ignored by the board tool — a candidate is not on the board yet by definition. 'Not reproduced/Fixed' is the one value the agent may set, and only over 'Proposed' — prefer `recheck`, which also records the build.

severityBranch.description: Which severity-decision-tree branch fired. QA-internal: bug-row.mjs renders it as a cell NOTE on the Summary cell; it NEVER enters the ticket body (severity does not exist on the board).

custom_fields.description: Redmine passthrough, sent as-is with the issue (board tool only).

recheck.description: Candidates funnel only: the latest re-check. result 'not-reproduced' sets 'Not reproduced/Fixed' over a default 'Proposed'; against a verdict the OWNER chose it never overwrites — the Sheet flags the row amber and bug-row.mjs lists it in needsOwner (BUG_REPORTS_RULES, candidates sheet).

build.description: '<flavour> @ <commit>' or the distribution build, plus who re-checked when it was not the agent.

ownerAsked.description: true when the owner could not reproduce it and asked the agent to re-check; a reproduced answer is coloured rose with a first line saying so.

note.description: How it was (or was not) reproduced, in one line — shown after the re-check line.

boardLine.description: Candidates funnel only: the paste-ready line of the Board checklist tab — N. *[<platform> - <area>]* <summary> *Screenshot:*|*Screen record:* <url> (REDMINE_WORKFLOW, checklist format).

area.description: 'Story x.y', or the broken area when no story fits.

onBoard.description: Candidates funnel only: the defect is ALREADY a point on the board — name it ('#<task> point 15'). Keeps it out of the Board checklist tab; AI Comments say so.

boardOverlap.description: Candidates funnel only: a board point covers PART of this defect — say which point and what it does and does not cover. The boardLine is then narrowed to the uncovered part.
